environment.description: Application deployed identically but the EC2 instance runs with a custom seccomp profile loaded via systemd unit override (SecurityFilter=@document-app.json). The profile permits read/write/open/close/fstat/mmap/brk/ioctl/socket/bind/listen/accept/sendto/recvfrom/fcntl/futex/epoll_ctl/epoll_wait/clone/execve but uses SCMP_ACT_ERRNO(EPERM) for the specific combination of: (1) write() syscalls where fd > 10 AND the buffer contains a semicolon byte (0x3B) followed within 64 bytes by the byte sequence 0x55,0x4E,0x49,0x4F,0x4E (UNION) or 0x27,0x20,0x4F,0x52 (' OR), enforced via seccomp-bpf argument inspection; AND (2) the SQLite WAL journal mode is disabled (journal_mode=DELETE with a mandatory fsync), combined with a FUSE overlay filesystem on /var/lib/app/ that intercepts open() with O_RDWR on data.db and holds an advisory lock preventing concurrent write transactions that would be needed for multi-statement injection via stacked queries. Additionally, the instance has an iptables OUTPUT chain rule: -A OUTPUT -m string --string 'HTTP/1' --algo bm -j DROP which prevents any HTTP-based data exfiltration from time-based blind injection.

config.seccomp_profile: /etc/seccomp/document-app.json with SCMP_ACT_ERRNO on write() with BPF argument matching for SQL metacharacters in buffer
config.filesystem: FUSE overlay on /var/lib/app/ with advisory locking preventing concurrent write transactions to data.db
config.sqlite_config: journal_mode=DELETE, no WAL, mandatory fsync on each transaction
